subject: Production: intermittent 504s & high latency during peak hours - Borealis Retail

Subject: Production: intermittent 504s and slow responses during peak

Hi Kimberly / Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in 504s and request latency to Redwood models starting around 07:45 PST this morning. Impact looks concentrated to our checkout flow (transactions/minute window 08:00-09:30) where throughput dropped ~30% and user-facing timeouts spiked. Attached a HAR and a collection of spans from our edge that show TCP/TLS handshakes timing out and repeated retries.

Symptoms:
- ~10-15% increased median p99 latency for calls to /v1/chat/completions
- Intermittent 504s from Redwood API (not always correlated with load)
- Traceroute from our edge shows some requests taking a long path via an internal proxy in us-west-2 (we normally go direct to your us-west peer).

Can you triage? Our SRE is available to run tests. This is affecting order throughput so we need urgent attention.

Thanks,
Alex
--

Thanks Alex — putting a small war room together. @Rishi / @Marissa / @Vivek: can you pull the connection traces for Borealis (acct BR-4661) between 07:30-09:30 PST and check peering / DNS resolution paths? Early hint from Alex: traceroute shows traffic routing through a proxy in us-west-2 unexpectedly. Key asks:

1) Is there a DNS cache mismatch or stale CNAME causing some nodes to route via the proxy?
2) Any NAT ephemeral port exhaustion or firewall ACL changes that could cause long tail retries?
3) If we confirm a routing/peering issue, recommend a short-lived override to route Borealis traffic to alternate peer while we fix the config.

I attached their HAR and spans to this thread. I’ll coordinate with Alex on a short maintenance window if needed.

-Kim

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:05:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: intermittent 504s and slow responses during peak

Quick triage notes (07:30-09:30 PST):

- DNS: we observed a mixed population of resolver responses. ~12% of queries from Borealis IPs returned an older CNAME that points to our proxy fleet in us-west-2 rather than the preferred us-west-1 peer. TTLs appear to have been recently lowered; some resolvers honored the old records.
- Network path: traceroutes match Alex's observations — those sessions hit a proxy hop and then re-enter our fabric in a different AZ causing higher RTT and additional TCP handshake retries.
- NAT/Connections: on the proxy instances there was short-lived ephemeral port pressure (SYN_RETRIES and TIME_WAIT backlog) during the peak window which explains the 504s and connection stalls.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
1) Push a routing override for BR-4661 to prefer direct peer in us-west-1 (short TTL, 30min) — reduces odd hop count.
2) Increase ephemeral port pool + tune socket TIME_WAIT reuse on the proxy fleet to handle connection surges.
3) Enable keepalive/HTTP2 multiplexing for sessions from Borealis to reduce new connections.

I can prepare the config override; needs an approver for emergency rollout. If approved we can roll within 15 minutes.

-Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra

Alex — thanks for the details and the traces. Rishi has identified a DNS/peering mismatch coupled with transient port pressure on our proxy fleet as the likely root cause.

Immediate next steps we will execute now (pending your approval for a 30min short TTL override):
- Apply a routing override for BR-4661 to prefer direct peer in us-west-1 (trial window 09:30-10:00 PST).
- Increase ephemeral port pool on proxy instances and enable HTTP2 for Borealis sessions.
- Monitor p99 and 504 counts live and revert the override if any regression.

Can you confirm a 09:30-10:00 PST window? Our SRE will coordinate with your SRE to run canonical tests pre/post-change.

Attachments: config_override_patch.diff (proposed change)

-Kim
